topicLeaks.text: "We never finished talking about that favor — we wandered off it. Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"We never finished talking about that favor — we left it mid-thought. You know?"
"We never finished talking about that personal stuff — we left it mid-thought. You doing okay?"

transcript.text: "I… ...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I was a wild food forager. Which means I'm good at noticing what everyone else walks past."
"Huh. I wouldn't have guessed that about you."
"I realize I don't actually know you. Who are you?"
"Good question." "You know what I miss? Columbus, Ohio rain. Specific rain. I'm allowed to be specific."
"We started on that question, then got onto themselves."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Yeah — Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Hands remember things the head forgets. Watch what yours do when you're not thinking."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About that question — So what's your plan here? Just... get through it? Anyway, that's me."
"Right, so — Honest. I can work with honest."
"What's your thing — what are you for?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Why — do I look useless to you?" A grin takes the sting out. "I was a lawyer. I manage."
"I think the asking matters more than the answer, out here."
"I realize I don't actually know you. Who are you?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "We should name this place. 'Camp' is what you call somewhere you're leaving."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"About that question — I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"What should I ask you for help with?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Taking things apart to see how they work. That's my thing. Everything else I'm figuring out like everyone."
"So — who are you, when nobody's watching?"
"Good question." "Every morning I wake up surprised. Like part of me still expects the old world. That is all."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
(Yeva speaks only 🇺🇦 Ukrainian. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.)
«Гей... ти розмовляєш українською? Ні? ...бляха.» "Thank you?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Так, так, саме так.» They nod back, slowly.
«Саме так. В точку.» (you catch 'точку' — point) They nod back, slowly.
«Правильно.» (you catch 'Правильно' — correct) They nod back, slowly.
«Так, ти правий.» (you catch 'правий' — right) They nod back, slowly.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
«Так, так, саме так.» (you catch 'Так' — yes) They nod back, slowly.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"What's your thing — what are you for?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I was a plumber. Which means I'm good at making things work with what's actually here."
"I realize I don't actually know you. Who are you?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Listen — You ever get a song stuck in your head with no way to play it? It's a special kind of torture."
"Right. That's what I figured — which is why I asked you, not them. That's the whole of it."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"About that question — Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."

"We started on that question, then got onto themselves. That's my read."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"A kitchen. Morning light. I must've been three."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"How are we with the neighbors, honestly?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I don't have more words for it. Some things just are."
"What small thing do you miss most?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Brussels, Belgium had this smell after rain — concrete and wet leaves. I'd forgotten it until just now, saying it out loud."
"We started on that question, then got onto the old world."
"Huh. I wouldn't have guessed that about you."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "the woman in her 20s keeps me sane. Everyone needs one person who'd notice if they stopped showing up."
"About the old world — we never finished."
"I miss to sit under a roof during rain. Funny — I still hope for it, just... translated."
"the woman in her 20s was a musician, before. You can still see it — the way they handle things."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"We're down to 7 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"You really want my take? ...Yeah. Okay. I think we're being tested."
"7 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. The creek's a twenty-minute walk — with two of us it's one trip, not three."
"Dawn, then. Bring something to carry — and thank you."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"Still on that favor. No point pretending otherwise."

They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.

"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
